title: A predictive closure of the biological carbon pump

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a transferable theory of how biological activity moves organic carbon from the sunlit ocean into deeper water, and how much of that carbon survives to each depth. A predictive closure would supply the process relationships needed by an ocean model to calculate export and its attenuation from environmental conditions and observed ecology, with parameters fixed before validation. Its defining achievement would be to explain modern conditions and predict an independently observed perturbation without retuning the processes responsible for the answer.

Export and transfer efficiency are distinct parts of this problem. Export describes carbon leaving a specified upper-ocean reference depth; transfer efficiency describes the fraction reaching a specified deeper depth. Predicting the first does not establish the second. The scope also needs to distinguish sinking particles from carbon carried by migrating organisms or physically transported organic matter. A successful closure for sinking particles would be an important accomplishment, but a claim to cover the biological carbon pump more broadly would require explicit treatment or justified exclusion of these other pathways.

significance.text: The biological carbon pump has a major background climatic and ecological role. Henson and coauthors describe biological export as maintaining atmospheric CO₂ approximately 200 ppm below a hypothetical world without that export flux, while supplying organic matter to the mesopelagic, or twilight-zone, ecosystem, including important fisheries. This counterfactual illustrates the importance of the existing pump; it does not quantify additional anthropogenic carbon uptake or carbon removal that the proposed breakthrough would enable.

If demonstrated, a transferable closure would turn uncertain representations of export and depth-dependent carbon loss into a capability for predicting their response to environmental change. This would improve the basis for assessing carbon sequestration and climate feedbacks because both the amount exported and its subsequent attenuation matter. The revolutionary advance would be predictive transfer between conditions, rather than merely a closer fit to the present ocean.

Conditional synthesis: coupled to independently constrained circulation, respiration and elemental stoichiometry, the closure could improve predictions of regenerated carbon and oxygen distributions. Those inventories depend on transport and biogeochemical accounting as well as biological export. Closing this component would therefore not close the full ocean carbon budget. Likewise, supplying carbon to the twilight zone does not by itself determine how efficiently that carbon passes through food webs into fish production.

missing_breakthrough.text: The missing capability is a mechanistic account of export and attenuation whose response to changing conditions is sufficiently constrained to predict a withheld state. Henson and coauthors identify particle fragmentation, zooplankton vertical migration, particle size spectra and temperature-dependent remineralization as priorities for better process representation. These are a mixture of incompletely represented mechanisms and uncertain parameterizations, rather than simply a collection of adjustable constants. Representing a process is insufficient unless its environmental drivers and response are also understood.

A central scientific barrier is that different mechanisms can compensate for one another and produce the same vertical carbon flux. Agreement with a flux profile can therefore conceal an incorrect process balance that fails when temperature, ecology or transport changes. Wang and Fennel's 2024 analysis explicitly identifies this ambiguity and argues for mechanistic understanding of export and attenuation within and below the euphotic zone. Independent process observations are needed alongside flux measurements to distinguish explanations that fit the same present-day data.

Proposed engineering requirement: integrate these relationships into a model that consistently accounts for carbon across the declared pathways and depths, while separating uncertainty in biological processes from uncertainty in circulation and elemental accounting. Validation must connect local process behavior to biome-scale and global behavior without introducing a new set of fitted remineralization or particle-size parameters for each test. Whether one formulation can achieve that breadth is the open objective, not an established result.

current_state.text: Henson and coauthors' Nature Geoscience Perspective, published on 8 April 2022, documents substantial disagreement among Earth system models that already represent biological carbon export. Across 19 CMIP6 models, the reported projected global export-flux response ranges from −41% to +1.8% under SSP5–8.5 to 2100, relative to each model's 1850–1900 mean. This is a scenario-specific range of model projections, not an observed response, a universal uncertainty interval or a forecast covering every emissions pathway.

The supplied review describes access to the 2022 article's abstract and ancillary material, plus a complete 19-page supplementary-information text; the main article body was unavailable. The supplementary caption supplies the scenario and baseline for the model comparison, but its figure was not visually inspected and was not used to independently check the numerical endpoints. The journal page identifies exactly six authors: Stephanie A. Henson, Charlotte Laufkötter, Shirley Leung, Sarah L. C. Giering, Hilary I. Palevsky and Emma L. Cavan. The earlier description of additional authors and exclusively abstract-level evidence was therefore inaccurate.

Wang and Fennel's intercomparison, published in Communications Earth & Environment on 23 July 2024, provides a more resolved diagnosis of model uncertainty. It compares 14 CMIP6 biogeochemical models and uses six representative models to partition uncertainty in historical simulations averaged over 2000–2014. Globally, export uncertainty dominates above approximately 900 m, while transfer-efficiency uncertainty dominates below that depth. The crossover has biome-dependent exceptions and describes this model analysis; it is not a universal observational boundary. The authors also caution that the selected models sample realized model diversity and need not span the full uncertainty of the real ocean.

The research notes attribute to a separate July 2024 model–data synthesis an ensemble-mean sinking export of 6.08 ± 1.17 Pg C yr⁻¹ at 100 m, an observational comparison range of roughly 5–12 Pg C yr⁻¹, and transfer efficiency to 1,000 m of 0.122 ± 0.041. No captured document for the cited DOI was available to the supplied review, so the source identity, numerical values, uncertainty definitions and precise transfer-efficiency convention could not be checked. These figures are retained as unverified research-note attributions, rather than established quantitative benchmarks. The missing evidence does not show that they are false.

The studies assessed in the supplied review document model disagreement, process-representation needs and ambiguity in inferring mechanisms from fluxes; they do not demonstrate the proposed untuned predictive closure. The supplied evidence also does not substantiate the broader research-note claim that process campaigns collectively established additional pumps without producing a climate-response law. Because the freshness record contains no subsequent assessment, these dated findings cannot establish whether the proposed capability remained unachieved on 1 November 2026.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: declare the covered export pathways, upper and lower reference depths, major biomes, parameter-calibration data and uncertainty model before validation. With one closure and parameters fixed in advance, reproduce modern export and depth-resolved transfer efficiency across every major biome within predeclared, uncertainty-aware tolerances. These are proposed acceptance conditions, not established community standards; their numerical tolerances remain to be specified.
completion_criteria.label: Fixed closure reproduces export and depth-resolved transfer across major biomes

completion_criteria.text: Validation should combine independent flux measurements with tracer, oxygen and process constraints, rather than treating agreement with one inventory or flux profile as sufficient. Circulation, respiration and stoichiometric uncertainties must be propagated when comparing carbon and oxygen inventories, because inventory errors do not translate directly into tolerances on export or transfer efficiency. The need for independent process constraints follows from the documented possibility that different mechanisms produce the same vertical flux.
completion_criteria.label: Independent flux and process constraints validate closure with propagated uncertainties

completion_criteria.text: Proposed predictive test: use the fixed closure to predict both the sign and magnitude of change in a warming experiment or natural perturbation withheld from calibration. Remineralization and particle-size relationships must remain fixed rather than being adjusted after seeing the outcome. Reproducible evaluation would require the equations, parameters, calibration and validation partitions, data processing and uncertainty calculations to be available for independent implementation or rerunning.
completion_criteria.label: Fixed closure predicts withheld perturbation’s sign and magnitude without retuning

completion_criteria.text: Proposed practical boundary: report performance separately by pathway, biome, depth and perturbation, including failures and conditions outside the calibration range. One successful withheld perturbation would demonstrate transferability over its tested conditions; multiple independent perturbations would establish broader evidence. No finite test suite establishes literal universality. Claims about regenerated carbon, oxygen, long-term sequestration or fisheries should be evaluated only with the additional transport and ecosystem capabilities those outcomes require.
completion_criteria.label: Report disaggregated performance, failures and limits of demonstrated transferability

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: OCE-09, A predictive theory of pelagic size structure and trophic transfer, has the closest overlap. Particle size, plankton ecology and migration can influence both carbon export and food-web transfer. OCE-03 targets carbon leaving the upper ocean and surviving to depth; OCE-09 targets size structure and transfer through trophic levels. Either predictive capability could be achieved without completing the other. Only OCE-09's title and the candidate's proposed boundary are supplied, so a more exact division of scope cannot be verified.

Roster-based synthesis: OCE-01, A closed theory of oceanic turbulent transport, and OCE-07, The stability class of the global overturning circulation, concern physical transport relevant to interpreting exported carbon and its subsequent distribution. Better transport predictions could strengthen biological-pump validation and inventory calculations. OCE-03 nevertheless addresses the biological export and attenuation relationships rather than resolving turbulent transport or overturning stability.

Roster-based synthesis: OCE-02, Synoptic sensing of the ocean interior, could provide broader observational constraints for validating export, attenuation and associated inventories. OCE-04, Persistent mobile operations at full ocean depth, and OCE-10, Basin-scale underwater positioning without surfacing, could support sustained or better-located measurements. These are potentially enabling observation and operations capabilities; achieving them would not itself establish a predictive biological closure.

Roster-based synthesis: OCE-05, Closure of ocean–crust fluid and biogeochemical exchange, addresses a different interface and set of carbon and chemical exchanges. OCE-06, A verified law of ice-shelf basal melting, concerns another ocean process whose environmental effects could interact with circulation and ecosystems. OCE-08, Continuous centimeter-level geodesy of the seismogenic seafloor, concerns seafloor deformation measurement. Their supplied titles establish distinct objectives, with no basis here for treating any as part of, or a substitute for, OCE-03.

change_log.change: Defined closure as transferable prediction of export and depth-dependent attenuation, with pathway scope explicitly unresolved.
change_log.reason: Integrates the research objective with the review's distinction between sinking particles, active migration and physically transported organic matter.

change_log.change: Added the 19-model ensemble, SSP5–8.5 scenario, 2100 horizon and 1850–1900 baseline to the −41% to +1.8% projection range.
change_log.reason: Prevents a dated, scenario-specific projection spread from being read as a universal or observed response.

change_log.change: Replaced the blanket assertion that processes remain adjustable with distinctions among missing mechanisms, uncertain parameterizations and poorly constrained environmental responses.
change_log.reason: Preserves the scientific barrier while reflecting the supplied review's more precise process diagnosis.

change_log.change: Clarified the approximately 200 ppm counterfactual and removed the unsupported attribution of the contemporary anthropogenic ocean sink.
change_log.reason: The supplied evidence supports background climatic importance, but not additional-removal potential or that sink attribution.

change_log.change: Made regenerated-carbon, oxygen and fisheries implications conditional on additional capabilities.
change_log.reason: Export closure alone does not determine transport, respiration, stoichiometry or trophic transfer.

change_log.change: Corrected the 2022 author list and access description, and expanded the scope and caveats of the 2024 intercomparison.
change_log.reason: The review identifies six authors, an available complete supplement, and uncertainty partitioning based on six representatives from 14 models using 2000–2014 historical simulations.

change_log.change: Retained the uncaptured synthesis's quantitative estimates as explicitly unverified attributions.
change_log.reason: Preserves potentially useful research detail without presenting unavailable evidence as verified or treating its absence as disproof.

change_log.change: Expanded completion criteria to include independent process constraints, uncertainty propagation, withheld perturbations, reproducibility and declared limits.
change_log.reason: A present-day fit can conceal compensating mechanisms, and finite validation demonstrates tested breadth rather than universality.

change_log.change: Separated dated evidence from the unresolved November 2026 status and described roster relationships as synthesis.
change_log.reason: The empty freshness record and title-only related-concept descriptions do not support stronger claims.

unresolved_issues: The proposal must decide whether it covers sinking particles alone or also active migration and physically transported organic matter, and define the associated reference depths.

DOI 10.1029/2024GB008156 has no captured source in the supplied evidence. Its identity, numerical estimates, uncertainty definitions and transfer-efficiency convention remain unchecked. The review's recommendation to remove those numbers was not adopted because the requested record calls for preserving unresolved quantitative detail with explicit qualification.
The evidence does not establish whether a qualifying predictive closure appeared after the assessed 2024 work and before 1 November 2026.
The broader claim about what process campaigns collectively established remains unsubstantiated by the supplied review and is not adopted as a finding.
Numerical validation tolerances, biome coverage, independent perturbations and a method for separating biological from circulation and stoichiometric uncertainty remain to be specified.
OCE-09's full definition and the other related concepts' detailed scopes were not supplied; their boundaries beyond the roster titles cannot be verified.

One 2024 supplementary extraction is truncated in the source index. No additional conclusion is drawn from its omitted material; the intercomparison findings used here follow the supplied review of the full article.

brief.title: Predicting how ocean life carries carbon into the deep
possible: Scientists could predict how much carbon ocean life carries below sunlit waters, how much reaches deeper water, and how that changes as the ocean warms. The same model would work across different ocean environments without being adjusted after seeing each result.
why: Carbon carried into the deep ocean helps regulate atmospheric carbon dioxide and supplies food to deeper ecosystems. Better predictions would help climate researchers assess how this carbon storage responds to environmental change.

sources.showed: Their synthesis found that climate models disagree about how carbon leaving the upper ocean will respond to climate change. They identified biological processes that models need to represent better.
sources.quote: Earth system models disagree on the projected response of the global export flux to climate change
sources.cited_for: The work establishes disagreement in climate projections and identifies processes that could help explain it.
sources.not_established: It does not demonstrate a model that predicts an independent environmental change without adjusting its biological relationships.

sources.showed: A later version of the same work.
This work combines models and observations to estimate sinking carbon leaving the upper ocean and the fraction reaching deeper water.
sources.cited_for: The work addresses estimates of sinking carbon transport and its survival with depth.
sources.not_established: Estimates of present carbon transport do not establish prediction under changed conditions without adjustment.

sources.showed: Their model comparison found that disagreement grows with depth. Uncertainty about carbon leaving the upper ocean matters most nearer the surface; uncertainty about the fraction surviving matters most deeper down.
sources.quote: On the global scale, uncertainty in carbon export dominates above 900 m and uncertainty in transfer efficiency below.
sources.cited_for: Predicting carbon leaving the upper ocean and predicting its survival at depth are separate, necessary challenges.
sources.not_established: Differences among these models do not span all real ocean uncertainty or demonstrate reliable prediction under environmental change.

shown: Henson and colleagues documented disagreement about future carbon transport. Wang and Fennel traced model disagreement to different sources at different depths. These studies diagnose weaknesses; neither demonstrates a model that passes an independent test of environmental change without adjustment.
missing: A model still needs to explain both carbon leaving sunlit waters and its survival at depth across major ocean environments with fixed parameters.
Independent measurements must distinguish biological mechanisms that can produce the same downward carbon flow.
The fixed model must predict the direction and size of a change excluded from its development.

milestones.label: A fixed model matches carbon transport across ocean environments
milestones.explanation: A model with parameters fixed beforehand would have to match modern carbon transport at successive depths across major ocean environments within declared tolerances. This would establish its breadth under present conditions.

milestones.label: Independent measurements confirm the processes behind the predictions
milestones.explanation: Independent carbon, oxygen and process measurements would have to agree after accounting for uncertain currents, biological carbon breakdown and elemental ratios. This would test whether matching carbon flows hides wrong mechanisms.

milestones.label: The unchanged model predicts an independent environmental change
milestones.explanation: The fixed model would have to predict the direction and size of a warming response or natural change excluded from development, with independently reproducible results. This would test prediction beyond familiar conditions.

milestones.label: Results reveal where predictions succeed and fail
milestones.explanation: Results would have to separate successes and failures by carbon pathway, ocean environment, depth and environmental change. This would define where the model works and where broader claims need further tests.

uncertain: It remains open whether the model can cover sinking particles, migrating organisms and carbon carried by moving water within the same framework.
Acceptable errors and the ocean environments and independent changes needed for a convincing test remain to be defined.
Success in a single environmental change would leave open how widely the same biological relationships apply.

page.title: Mechanistic prediction of the biological carbon pump
page.definition: A mechanistic model predicts organic-carbon export below sunlit waters and its fate at depth through sinking, migrating organisms and physical transport. Its equations and parameters predict independent environments and an observed environmental perturbation without refitting; for sinking particles, transfer efficiency is deeper flux divided by export flux.

goal.need: Biological export maintains atmospheric CO₂ about 200 ppm below a hypothetical world without that flux. A comparison of 14 CMIP6 models, with uncertainty partitioned using six representatives, found export uncertainty dominant above about 900 m and transfer-efficiency uncertainty below, globally, for historical simulations averaged over 2000–2014. Predicting carbon storage therefore requires constraints on both export and subsequent carbon loss.

figures.caption: RECCAP2 model estimates of sinking-carbon transport, averaged over 1995–2018.
rows: Transfer efficiency: 1,000 m flux / 100 m flux
figures.note: Standard deviations describe intermodel spread. Model counts are inferred from Table 1 and Figure 3's exclusions. Depths use different model subsets; transfer efficiencies are calculated within models before averaging.

statements.quote: develop a predictive understanding of the export and fate of global ocean primary production
understand how biological carbon export, remineralization, dissolution, sequestration, and BCP efficiency changes with natural and anthropogenic variability

completion.title: A fixed model predicts observed changes in biological carbon export and transfer efficiency.
completion.criterion: Using unchanged process equations and parameters, a mechanistic model reproduces export and depth-resolved transfer across independent ocean environments and predicts the sign and magnitude of their response to an observed environmental perturbation withheld from development. It accounts for sinking particles, migrating organisms and physical transport. Predicted fluxes and changes fall within independently estimated observational uncertainty intervals, with uncertainties in circulation and elemental ratios propagated. This is an Atlas acceptance convention; no external numerical tolerance or mandatory test count was found.
completion.set_by: Technology Atlas; operational interpretation of the EXPORTS prediction goal.
completion.basis: Searches of the EXPORTS science and implementation plans, the COMICS programme paper, NOAA's 2025 ocean-carbon plan and recent model studies found no shared completion benchmark, error tolerance or untuned perturbation protocol. This test operationalizes the quoted prediction goal. One perturbation establishes transfer only over its tested conditions.

milestones.title: A local twilight-zone carbon budget balances within observational uncertainties.
milestones.criterion: Reconcile organic-carbon sources and sinks within observational uncertainty for a defined layer and sampling period. At one Porcupine Abyssal Plain site, sampled from 8 July 2009 to 13 August 2009, Giering et al. reported 50–1,000 m sources of 68–116 and sinks of 48–167 mg C m⁻² d⁻¹. Their balance assumed steady state. Oliver et al. (2025) found in a global model that subannual sources and sinks usually do not balance.
milestones.set_by: NERC COMICS programme, Synthesis and modeling; uncertainty convention demonstrated by Giering et al. (2014).

milestones.title: A food-web model reproduces observed twilight-zone carbon flux and respiration budgets.
milestones.criterion: Reproduce observed twilight-zone carbon flux and respiration budgets using a food-web process model. COMICS specifies no numerical residual tolerance. Related evidence published on 5 August 2022: NEMURO_BCP was constrained with 30 data types from 49 experiments on 11 cruises in four regions and evaluated against withheld thorium-234 and nitrogen-isotope data. Export biases remained in the Costa Rica Dome; this study does not establish reproduction of a complete respiration budget.
milestones.set_by: NERC COMICS programme, 2016 programme paper, Synthesis and modeling.
milestones.threshold_quote: reproduce the budgets of interior flux and respiration

milestones.title: A global ocean model reproduces observed nutrient, carbon and oxygen distributions at equilibrium.
milestones.criterion: The process formulation reproduces global nutrient, carbon and oxygen fields in an equilibrated three-dimensional circulation model. COMICS specifies a transport-matrix calculation without a numerical error threshold. On 31 January 2026, Li et al. reported a seasonal global model of all three export pathways, with 42 parameters optimized in four configurations. This supplies a fitted global state estimate; independent reproduction of the tracer fields remains a separate test.
milestones.set_by: NERC COMICS programme, 2016 programme paper, Synthesis and modeling.
milestones.threshold_quote: ability to reproduce the global tracer field

milestones.title: An Earth system model runs process-derived export parameterizations tested against field data.
milestones.criterion: An Earth system model incorporates mechanistic export and attenuation parameterizations tested against campaign and historical observations, with evaluation in other ocean regions and of the coupled biogeochemical fields. EXPORTS gives no numerical pass tolerance. Published on 4 July 2024, the RECCAP2 comparison demonstrates evaluation of global sinking-particle fluxes; it does not establish the full process-model-to-Earth-system-model validation chain.
milestones.set_by: NASA-supported EXPORTS Science Plan Writing Team, 2015 science plan, section 6.6.
milestones.threshold_quote: incorporate these new, tested parameterizations into well characterized Earth System Models

not_found: No published demonstration satisfying the complete fixed-parameter perturbation test was identified through 14 November 2026.
